cases.title: Packing-fraction-dependent organization in the two-dimensional hard-disk model

participants.value: Structureless hard disks in a two-dimensional periodic square; source calculations use N=256^2, 512^2 and up to 1024^2.

changedFactor.value: Packing fraction eta: source scan identifies approximate liquid-hexatic coexistence from 0.700 to 0.716, a hexatic example at 0.718 and an upper transition near 0.720.

observable.value: Computed equilibrium equation of state, coexistence patterns, interface scaling and positional/bond-orientational correlations.

response.value: At eta=0.718 positional correlations decay exponentially on a scale of about 100 disk radii, with very slow orientational decay. Near eta=0.720 positional decay is approximately algebraic, near r^-1/3 over the resolved range.

conditions.value: Constant-NV periodic-square hard-disk calculation using an event-chain algorithm with global balance; correlation analysis uses the measured structure-factor peak.

boundary.value: Finite periodic square, stated disk counts and hard-core interaction model; finite-size effects remain near the upper transition.

controls.value: Crystal/liquid initial conditions, autocorrelation, finite-size checks and the supplement Gaussian sampling-error procedure; structure-factor peak is found numerically rather than imposed from a perfect lattice.

interpretation.value: The source interprets combined observables as first-order liquid-hexatic coexistence and a continuous hexatic-solid transition in this specified entropic model.

uncertainty.value: Transition locations are approximate and source-specific; finite-size effects remain. Orientational data at eta=0.718 alone do not resolve quasi-long-range versus true long-range behavior.

observations.statement: The reported equilibrium calculations find coexistence patterns and an equation of state supporting approximate liquid-hexatic coexistence over eta=0.700-0.716.
At eta=0.718 positional correlations have an approximately 100-disk-radius exponential scale; near eta=0.720 decay becomes approximately algebraic near r^-1/3 over the resolved range.
The source assigns first-order liquid-hexatic coexistence and a continuous hexatic-solid transition using the joint finite-box evidence and theoretical framework.
No physical melting or nucleation timescale is established by the algorithmic disk-displacement clock.

limitations: Author arXiv v2 and supplement were read; final published full text was not obtained. Supplement code was read without execution and linked configurations were not downloaded.
No pressure contact-fit, configuration/covariance analysis, equation-of-state integration or independent simulation replay was performed.
Monte Carlo displacement time is not a physical kinetic law. The null timeScale records that a physical timescale is inapplicable to this admitted equilibrium comparison.
Main text, supplement, pressure, morphology and correlation analyses are one computational study; sampled configurations are not independent publications.

cases.title: Finite persistence and heat-treatment conversion of rapidly cooled icosahedral Al-Mn

participants.value: Rapidly cooled Al-Mn alloy, especially Al-14 at.% Mn, with finite icosahedrally ordered grains; the converted product is reported as Al6Mn.

changedFactor.value: Thermal-treatment protocol: 6 h at 300 C, 1 h at 350 C, or 1 h at 400 C.

observable.value: Selected-area electron diffraction, dark-field contrast, convergent-beam microdiffraction, powder diffraction and reported annealing response.

response.value: No detectable subsequent crystallization after 6 h at 300 C or 1 h at 350 C; conversion to stable Al6Mn after 1 h at 400 C.

conditions.value: Reported rapidly cooled Al-Mn preparation and separate finite annealing protocols; keep treatment duration and temperature together.

boundary.value: Finite alloy grains up to about 2 micrometres; the three anneals do not determine an equilibrium transition temperature or universal lifetime.

timeScale.value: Observation/treatment windows: 6 h at 300 C, 1 h at 350 C and 1 h at 400 C; no fitted lifetime distribution.

controls.value: Dark-field whole-grain contrast, small-volume convergent-beam microdiffraction and Cu K-alpha powder diffraction test a conventional multiple-twinning explanation.

interpretation.value: Finite icosahedral order and protocol-dependent metastability; morphology and segregation support the source growth interpretation without a measured latent heat or quantitative kinetic coefficient.

uncertainty.value: No infinite correlation length or unique atom arrangement is established; finite anneal outcomes do not quantify a transition rate or barrier.

observations.statement: The selected material shows related diffraction patterns with six fivefold, ten threefold and fifteen twofold axes, with orientational correlation across finite grains up to about 2 micrometres.
No detectable subsequent crystallization is reported after 6 h at 300 C or 1 h at 350 C.
Conversion to stable Al6Mn is reported after 1 h at 400 C.
The source interprets the prepared phase as metastable under its annealing protocols; morphology and segregation motivate a first-order growth interpretation.
The selected observations do not provide a measured kinetic barrier, quantitative rate coefficient, latent heat or equilibrium phase-boundary curve.

limitations: All published pages were read; no raw diffraction-intensity refinement, calorimetry, new imaging or kinetic replay was performed.
Different treatment durations and temperatures must remain attached to their outcomes; 400 C is not an equilibrium transition temperature inferred from this record.
No detected conversion is a finite observational result, not zero transition probability or indefinite persistence.
Diffraction controls, morphology and annealing results are one publication rather than independent replications.

cases.title: Host/isotopologue-dependent cryogenic hydroxymethylene decay, with a separate tunnelling model

participants.value: Assigned trans-H-C-OH and H-C-OD in cryogenic host/product mixtures following glyoxylic-acid pyrolysis; formaldehyde and other products are also present.

changedFactor.value: Host matrix, temperature and isotopologue are separate preparation axes: reported H points use Ar/Kr/Xe/N2 at 11 K, Ar at 15 K and Ar/Kr at 20 K; D has only a qualitative non-decay statement.

observable.value: Assigned H-C-OH infrared-band loss in shielded dark storage, sampled every 30 min; qualitative persistence of assigned H-C-OD bands.

response.value: Reported H half-lives in hours: 11 K Ar 1.8, Kr 2.0, Xe 2.3, N2 7.0; 15 K Ar 1.9; 20 K Ar 1.7 and Kr 2.0. D bands are unchanged over an unspecified extended observation period.

conditions.value: High-vacuum flash pyrolysis at 1000 C followed by immediate trapping with excess cryogenic Ar/Kr/Xe/N2; dark kinetics are shielded from external light and separate from visible-light assignment tests.

resources.value: Excess host matrix traps the pyrolysis products; no continuing resource-replenishment experiment is admitted.

boundary.value: Cryogenic host/product mixture rather than pure isolated gas; only reported host/temperature cells are admitted, with other table cells missing.

timeScale.value: H half-lives range from 1.7 to 7.0 h across reported cells, with 30 min spectral sampling. D observation duration and experimental D half-life remain unspecified.

controls.value: Dark shielding, separate host/isotopologue comparisons, and separate irradiation/difference spectra used for assignment rather than merged with dark kinetics.

interpretation.value: The associated reduced reaction-path/WKB calculation interprets H loss via tunnelling and predicts a near-0-K H half-life of 122 min and D half-life over 1200 yr; these are theoretical outputs.

uncertainty.value: No table uncertainty intervals, replicate counts or detection limit are provided; no numerical experimental D half-life or isotope-rate ratio follows. Reduced WKB dynamics are not a full-dimensional calculation.

observations.statement: The source observes time-dependent H-C-OH infrared-band loss in the declared dark host-matrix preparations. Its first-order fitted half-lives are retained separately as a measurement inference.
Assigned H-C-OD bands are reported unchanged over an unspecified extended observation period.
The source reduced reaction-path/WKB calculation predicts a near-0-K H half-life of 122 min and a D half-life over 1200 yr.
No numerical experimental D half-life or kinetic isotope ratio is established; the model does not supply a matrix-specific account of all four hosts.

First-order analysis of the measured H-C-OH band loss gives source half-lives: at 11 K Ar 1.8 h, Kr 2.0 h, Xe 2.3 h, N2 7.0 h; at 15 K Ar 1.9 h; at 20 K Ar 1.7 h and Kr 2.0 h. These are source fits, not a new fit or directly measured D lifetime.

limitations: Selected published main-text/Methods passages and selected actual publisher-supplement passages were read; most coordinate/energy tables and raw spectra were not reanalysed.
The experiment and associated calculation are different evidence roles within one publication. The 1200 yr D value is theoretical, not an observed retention window.
Missing temperature/host cells, errors, replicates, detection limits and numeric D observation window remain unknown.
Visible-light photochemistry is separate from dark kinetics; IR loss does not directly count tunnelling events or certify every quantum state.
This is a persistence/chemical-conversion case. It does not independently demonstrate switching between collective organizational regimes.
This mixed-evidence case retains experiment and computation as distinct observation kinds and study contexts within one shared publication group.

cases.title: Screened repulsion and finite null long-range attraction in isolated charged-colloid pairs

participants.value: Isolated aqueous polystyrene-sulfate sphere pairs with radius 326 nm in a controlled thin glass cell.

changedFactor.value: Relative separation after release from optical tweezers; initial separations are 1.5 or 1.7 micrometres.

observable.value: Finite pair-release trajectories and transition probabilities: 796 trajectories, 6502 pooled initial/final separation samples, 57 nm bins and 1/30 s transition interval.

response.value: Transition-model inference reports screened repulsion with effective charge 1991 +/-150 elementary-charge units and screening length 161 +/-10 nm, and no statistically significant long-range attraction in the resolved preparation/range.

conditions.value: Dilute aqueous isolated pairs in a 3-4 micrometre glass-cell gap, with ion-exchange reservoirs and argon flushing; release only with no nearby other particles.

boundary.value: Finite resolved pair-separation range and stated glass-cell preparation; concentrated-cell crystals are a different ionic-purity control and not isolated-pair retention.

timeScale.value: The transition-matrix interval is 1/30 s; this is not a measured pair-assembly lifetime.

controls.value: No nearby third particle during pair release; ionic-contamination controls and a separate concentrated-cell crystal preparation used to assess ionic purity.

interpretation.value: The finite release data are mapped to a stationary distribution under a time-homogeneous Smoluchowski model, then to U=-kB*T*log(p_eq) up to a constant; the inferred potential is not a direct equilibrium histogram.

uncertainty.value: Mean separation uncertainty is 50 nm; localization broadens the potential and biases inferred charge. Reported fit errors have no newly verified coverage/covariance, and actual experimental temperature is not established by a 25 C reference constant.

observations.statement: The source acquires finite isolated-pair release trajectories, which underlie its transition-model potential inference.
Under the source model, the finite trajectories support screened repulsion with effective charge 1991 +/-150 elementary-charge units and screening length 161 +/-10 nm.
The analysis finds no statistically significant long-range attraction in its resolved preparation and separation range.
The separate concentrated-cell crystals persisting for months do not establish an isolated-pair assembly lifetime or persistent bound state.

limitations: Published source passages and the finite analysis were reviewed; no raw video, calibration replay, independent charge assay or new covariance analysis was supplied.
The transition model assumes spherical separation dependence and omits hydrodynamic coupling; projection, finite bins and the outer boundary affect inference.
No statistically significant attraction is a finite range/preparation result, not all-colloid exclusion of attraction.
The source 25 C Bjerrum reference value does not establish the actual experimental temperature.
Trajectories, inferred stationary distribution, potential and fit parameters share one source study. The concentrated purity-control crystals are a different preparation.
This is a deliberate retrospective limit case for the persistence framework, not positive evidence of an assembly barrier.

cases.title: Size-dependent finite growth/shrink of post-shear colloidal crystal nuclei

participants.value: Sterically stabilized weakly charged PMMA particles after shear melting, with classifier-defined crystal-like nuclei and liquid surroundings.

changedFactor.value: Classified nucleus population M in growth/shrink comparisons at volume fraction 0.47; separate time-series and interface-fit examples use other stated volume fractions.

observable.value: Finite confocal particle-position histories, classifier-defined nucleus growth/shrink, nonspherical rough shapes and small-nucleus area statistics.

response.value: At volume fraction 0.47, growth-minus-shrink probability changes sign across 60<M<160 particles. Nuclei have ordered cores, rough diffuse exteriors and source-inferred effective gamma approximately 0.027*kB*T/a^2.

conditions.value: Shear-melted 50 microlitre suspension in density/index-matched decahydronaphthalene/cyclohexylbromide; weakly charged nearly-hard spheres observed away from treated walls.

boundary.value: Finite 58 by 55 by 20 cubic-micrometre confocal volume with about 4000 particles; growth/shrink analysis excludes nuclei too near its edge. Classifier and visibility limits constrain the admitted critical range.

timeScale.value: A separate volume-fraction-0.45 snapshot series spans 20, 43, 66 and 89 min after shear melting; duration/frame count for the 0.47 critical-size measurement is unspecified.

controls.value: Declared l=6 bond-order thresholds, imaging away from walls, edge exclusion for nucleus histories and simulated order-reference histograms broadened to experimental resolution.

interpretation.value: Finite growth/shrink yields a preparation/classifier-dependent critical range; spherical-equivalent radius and area-statistics gamma are model-assisted inferences, not direct universal nucleation or surface-tension constants.

uncertainty.value: Reference packing calibration, local-order thresholds, finite visibility, rough nonspherical shape and incomplete high-density equilibration constrain inference; unique-event counting and universal nucleation rates are not established.

observations.statement: At source volume fraction 0.47, finite subcritical nuclei frequently shrink and growth-minus-shrink probability changes sign across 60<M<160 classified particles.
At source volume fraction 0.45, snapshots at 20, 43, 66 and 89 min show finite post-shear structural evolution.
The source infers a spherical-equivalent critical radius about 6.2*a and an effective interface free energy about 0.027*kB*T/a^2; the volume-fraction-0.445 example gives 0.026*kB*T/a^2.
No universal critical population, complete homogeneous-nucleation rate or directly measured exact equilibrium surface tension is established by these classifier-dependent post-shear data.

limitations: Published scientific main text and selected nucleation/interface passages were read; no raw confocal tracking, new event accounting or interface-fit replay was performed.
The 60<M<160 range is conditional on preparation and classifier, not a universal component minimum; classifier bonds denote neighbor directions rather than chemical bonds.
At higher densities immediate growth limited observation of early critical-nucleus formation. This missing observation is not a negative result.
Snapshots at 0.45, critical-size inference at 0.47 and the 0.445 area-fit example remain distinct source preparations; their clocks/results cannot be silently pooled.
The system is weakly charged and nearly hard-sphere-like; it is not Bernard two-dimensional structureless hard disks. No numerical density or critical-size transfer is justified.
Nucleus histories, structure fits and inferred interface cost share one study; repeated frames are not automatically independent events.
Continuing resource supply and its role in nucleus persistence were not reviewed as a controlled factor in these selected source claims.

cases.title: Field-selected AlScN film state with transverse piezoelectric sign reversal and finite retention

participants.value: Sputtered c-axis-oriented polycrystalline AlScN capacitor films; focus on Al0.64Sc0.36N before/after transverse-bending response.

changedFactor.value: Applied polarization reversal: selected x=0.36 direct transverse comparison uses a 0.1 Hz unipolar sine reaching -200 V over 60 s at room temperature.

observable.value: Direct transverse bending charge, switching/non-switching electrical response and polarity-selective etch contrast in distinct source subsamples.

response.value: Effective transverse e31,f changes from -2.90 to +2.76 C/m^2 after the stated reversal. A separate short-circuit pulse-retention preparation has no resolved back-switching loss up to 10^5 s, while non-switching charge is not exactly zero.

conditions.value: Substrate-constrained film with AlN/Pt bottom and patterned Pt top electrodes; direct transverse response uses 4-point bending and 16 mm^2 electrodes. Selected x=0.36 film is 600 nm thick.

resources.value: External field waveform selects the state; bending supplies the direct transverse readout. Retention uses short-circuited intervals between read pulses.

boundary.value: Finite oriented-film, electrode, axis and loading conventions; composition series, etch, loops, bending and retention are distinct subsamples within one publication.

timeScale.value: Selected reversal lasts 60 s; separate retention comparison uses 2 ms read pulses and intervals up to 10^5 s.

controls.value: Modified bipolar/unipolar leakage controls at 711/411 Hz; switching/non-switching pulses; switched/as-deposited etch regions after electrode removal with 50 nm overetch; before/after direct transverse measurement.

interpretation.value: Multiple readouts support the source ferroelectric classification and finite state-associated electromechanical sign control; a complete atomic reversal pathway is not directly established.

uncertainty.value: Leakage correction assumptions and finite distortions remain; readouts are not identical specimens or independent replications. No new error bars, raw-current replay or quantitative longitudinal coefficient is admitted; printed longitudinal corrections 0.85/0.83 disagree.

observations.statement: For the selected Al0.64Sc0.36N thin-film direct bending preparation, e31,f changes from -2.90 to +2.76 C/m^2 after the stated one-minute room-temperature reversal.
The separate short-circuited retention protocol finds no resolved loss attributable to back-switching up to 10^5 s between 2 ms read pulses; non-switching charge is not exactly zero.
Corrected electrical responses, polarity-selective etching and transverse response reversal support the source ferroelectric classification beyond a P-E loop alone.
No in-situ atomic reversal trajectory, every-grain switching certification, infinite retention or universal film coefficient is established.

limitations: Author arXiv v2 main text and selected supporting information were read; final publisher full-text identity was not verified.
The modified leakage correction assumes frequency-independent leakage and no switching in repeated non-switching sweeps; small distortions remain.
Loops, etching, bending and retention involve distinct source subsamples and cannot be represented as the same physical token or independent studies.
The retained coefficient is transverse e31,f under film/substrate constraints, not d33 or a universal bulk constant. The separate longitudinal correction discrepancy remains unresolved.
Finite retention does not establish infinite stability, device endurance or a continuously observed zero-field trace.
No raw-current/etch-image replay, complete atomic mechanism or independent replication was performed. This source group is used as a retrospective challenge, not prospectively unseen validation.

cases.title: Condition-dependent lymphotactin folds and construct-bounded responses

participants.value: Recombinant human lymphotactin WT; source-assigned Ltn10-like monomer and Ltn40-like dimer; CC3/W55D variants; heparin; XCR1-expressing HEK293 cells.

changedFactor.value: Temperature/NaCl in WT NMR preparations; WT versus engineered variants in separate assays; heparin addition to WT or CC3.

observable.value: Solution NMR populations/exchange peaks and NOE restraints; Trp55 fluorescence; heparin chromatography/titration; normalized cellular calcium response.

response.value: WT NMR populations shift with conditions. WT/CC3 elicit XCR1 calcium response, while W55D has no reported agonist response over 50–750 nM. Heparin suppresses WT signaling with Ltn40-like fluorescence, while CC3 resists this effect.

conditions.value: NMR: 20 mM sodium phosphate, pH 6.0, 90% H2O/10% D2O; Ltn40 structure inferred at 40 C without added NaCl. Functional constructs/solutions differ from the Ltn(2–93) NMR preparation.

resources.value: Supplied recombinant protein constructs, ligand/heparin, buffers and prepared receptor-expressing cells.

boundary.value: Solution structure and cellular assays are different preparations. Methods conflict M63A/M72A versus M63V/M72A. No intact-animal switching demonstration.

controls.value: WT/CC3/W55D comparisons, source carbachol normalization, WT/CC3 responses with and without heparin, and subsequent CC3 activation of the same cells.

interpretation.value: Condition-dependent alternative folds and a ligand-sensitive response are supported within source preparations. Variant comparisons change sequence and conformation together; fluorescence/calcium are proxies.

uncertainty.value: No new NMR ensemble, exchange-rate fit, functional uncertainty or pure-conformation causal effect reconstructed. Earlier approximately 100 ms exchange statement and near-equal physiological-condition populations contain inherited inputs.

observations.statement: WT spectra contain two signal sets and exchange peaks; temperature and salt shift their populations.
NOE-constrained analysis assigns an Ltn40 dimeric fold distinct from the Ltn10 chemokine-like fold.
WT/CC3 calcium responses differ from the absent reported W55D agonist response in the tested 50–750 nM range.
Heparin changes WT fluorescence and suppresses its calcium response; CC3 resists the effect and activates the same cells after WT suppression.
These different constructs and assay conditions do not isolate a pure conformational intervention on otherwise identical WT molecules.

limitations: Do not merge solution and cellular preparations into an identical-conformation intervention
Sequence/construct differences, fluorescence proxy and heparin aggregation/solution effects constrain mechanism
Supplement and raw NMR restraints unread; prior studies and MD refinement are not independent replications

cases.title: Alpha-lytic protease: fitted rates and conditional kinetic metastability

participants.value: Alpha-lytic protease I and native N; WT refolding/activity preparations, inactive S195A unfolding preparations, and supplied Pro in a separate catalyzed protocol.

changedFactor.value: Incubation time and temperature; denaturant concentration; separate Pro-catalyzed folding protocol.

observable.value: Calibrated catalytic activity after pepsin treatment; fluorescence/CD unfolding responses; fitted/extrapolated rates and rate-ratio free-energy inference.

response.value: At 4 C the source reports kf=(1.18 +/- 0.06)e-11 s^-1 and zero-denaturant extrapolated ku=(1.8 +/- 0.2)e-8 s^-1. Source rate-ratio inference favors I over native N by 4.0 +/- 0.1 kcal/mol at 4 C.

conditions.value: Uncatalyzed conversion: 10 mM potassium acetate, pH 5, 4/25 C. Pro protocol: 20 mM potassium phosphate, pH 7.2, 4 C, Pro:I at least 15:1. WT activity-loss control at 0.98 M guanidinium.

resources.value: Prepared enzyme states, supplied Pro for the separate protocol, pepsin selection, native-enzyme calibration and assay reagents.

boundary.value: Most unfolding uses S195A while refolding activity uses WT. Protocol pH/buffer differ. Practical I/N equilibrium was not directly sampled.

timeScale.value: Rates and extrapolated half-times characterize source models; millennial folding or year-scale persistence were not directly timed incubations. Exact acquisition window is not reconstructed.

controls.value: Native calibration, WT activity control and initial-rate restriction retaining I within 10% of its initial value.

interpretation.value: Under the source reversible-state/rate model, native functional persistence is interpreted through a large kinetic barrier despite I being thermodynamically favored.

uncertainty.value: Printed rate/free-energy uncertainties retain source conventions; zero-denaturant unfolding is extrapolated. Variant equivalence, raw fits and complete covariance were not independently validated.

observations.statement: Activity-calibrated initial-rate and denaturant-dependent spectroscopy analysis yield the source kf and extrapolated ku, not directly observed multi-year waiting times.
The source rate-ratio model favors I over N and interprets the native state as kinetically persistent.
Native functional persistence does not establish native I/N ground-state preference in this preparation; the source conditional inference points the other way.

limitations: Reversible I/N model and zero-denaturant extrapolation required
WT/S195A structural equivalence and inherited native-Pro binding inputs not independently verified
No raw regression/calorimetry replay; figures not raster-checked; no universal energy landscape or evolutionary mechanism

cases.title: CAPN: negative cooperativity and distal NMR response

participants.value: Prepared His6-tagged E. coli CAPN residues 1–138 homodimer and cAMP; source-assigned apo, nominal 1:1 and 2:1 cAMP:dimer preparations.

changedFactor.value: Supplied cAMP in the fixed-construct NMR ligand series and a separate ITC titration.

observable.value: Chemical shifts, relaxation/dispersion, amide H/D exchange and integrated ITC heat fitted with a sequential-site model.

response.value: Source sequential Kd values 0.04 and 4 micromolar imply less favorable second binding overall. First ligation changes remote motion signatures; second ligation broadly suppresses them and increases exchange protection.

conditions.value: NMR: 30 C, 600 MHz, typically 0.4 mM protein, representative 0.05/0.4/1.05 mM checks; complete solution/pD not reconstructed. ITC: 30 C, 30 micromolar protein, 0.6 mM titrant, 50 mM potassium phosphate pH 6.0, 500 mM KCl, 1 mM TCEP.

resources.value: Supplied purified isotope-labeled CAPN, cAMP, buffers and instrument preparations.

boundary.value: CAPN lacks full CAP DNA-binding domain. NMR and ITC are distinct samples/contexts within one publication. No DNA binding, transcription, catalytic turnover or cellular adaptation measured.

timeScale.value: NMR analysis distinguishes source slow/fast motion signatures, but no independently reconstructed common observation window or exact new residue-rate table is admitted.

controls.value: Common ligand-series construct/temperature, source identical exchange conditions, and representative NMR concentration controls.

interpretation.value: Site-resolved NMR plus sequential-site calorimetric fitting support the source negative-cooperativity and distal-response interpretation. Entropy decomposition is an additional model, not the same observable as total ITC entropy.

uncertainty.value: Nominal mixing does not ensure pure occupancy; Figure 7 Kd uncertainties unprinted. Sequential constants need state/statistical convention. Order-parameter entropy estimates assume uncorrelated motions; pathway is not uniquely identified.

observations.statement: The ligand series changes subunit signal sets and distal NMR motion/exchange signatures.
The source sequential-site ITC fit reports first/second Kd 0.04/4 micromolar and less favorable second-step total free energy.
The combined NMR/ITC source interpretation is dynamics-mediated negative cooperativity; conformational entropy values are conditional upper-bound model estimates.
The data do not resolve a unique communication pathway or prove purely entropy-only causation.

canonicalFunctionalRelations.assertion: The source ligand-series comparison changes amide-exchange protection under its stated identical exchange conditions.
Changing supplied cAMP in the matched source NMR protocol changes remote relaxation readouts; no unique communication mechanism is inferred.

limitations: Nominal stoichiometry does not prove pure occupancy populations
Sequential constants need state/combinatorial convention; not Hill coefficient or direct coupling-energy measurement
NMR/ITC and entropy model belong to one source group; no independent replication
Small remote chemical shifts do not establish zero structural displacement; pathway unresolved

cases.title: GOx/HRP nanocages: coupled activity and mechanism controls

participants.value: Commercial GOx/HRP, oligonucleotide-linked synthetic DNA full/half cages, glucose and ABTS reporter substrates.

changedFactor.value: Co-caged pair, separately full-caged enzymes, separate half-cages, and uncaged enzymes with/without empty cage.

observable.value: Separate TEM/label-colocalization/photobleaching characterization and 410 nm coupled ABTS absorbance activity traces.

response.value: Figure 3 source-normalized coupled activity is approximately 8-fold co-caged, 4-fold separately full-caged and 3-fold half-caged against the stated uncaged-pair plus empty-cage reference.

conditions.value: Nominal 1 nM enzyme/preparation; 1 mM glucose, 2 mM ABTS, 1xTBS pH 7.5; bulk Methods 1 mM MgCl2. Complete base TBS composition and common active fraction not reconstructed.

resources.value: Supplied commercial enzymes, synthetic DNA scaffold, conjugation/purification and substrates; nominal internal cage dimensions 20 by 20 by 17 nm.

boundary.value: Characterization and activity are separate preparations. Confinement is not the only varying property. Single-molecule G6pDH and conflicting protease protocols are outside this activity comparison.

controls.value: Separate full/half cages, empty-cage and no-cage references; SI fresh, same-thermal-program and substrate-background controls; Figure 3 SD of at least three replicates.

interpretation.value: Source-defined preparation changes accompany a coupled assay response. Separate cages also increase signal; co-cage enhancement alone does not uniquely establish substrate channeling or proximity-only action.

uncertainty.value: Source approximate normalizations are not new turnover fits. Active fractions, labeling/calibration, assembly/purification and local environment are not individually matched. Exact pair occupancy is not established for every cascade cage.

observations.statement: Source morphology/label association supports loading and scaffold association under its separate characterization protocols.
Source controls compare co-caged, separate full/half-caged and uncaged preparations in the stated coupled reporter assay.
The source reports increased normalized coupled activity, including increases for separate cages and half-cages.
The activity comparison does not isolate direct substrate channeling, reduced intermediate escape or a uniquely geometric proximity mechanism.

canonicalFunctionalRelations.assertion: The combined co-caged/separate/uncaged preparation intervention changes the measured coupled activity under the stated assay; no isolated channeling mechanism follows.

limitations: Nominal concentration matching does not match active fractions, conjugation, purification or local environment
Separate cages also raise signal; co-cage enhancement does not uniquely establish channeling, retention, hydration ordering or proximity-only mechanism
Source loading estimates do not establish exact GOx/HRP pair occupancy in every activity cage
Main/SI protease conditions conflict; no persistence/protection result admitted here

cases.title: Ddx4: reversible demixing, tracer mobility and DNA partition

participants.value: Supplied Ddx4N1 residues 1–236; separate fluorescent Ddx4YFP/CFP tracers; separate labeled 32-base ssDNA/32-bp dsDNA preparations.

changedFactor.value: Cooling/reheating in the thermal sample; local photobleaching in FRAP; ssDNA/dsDNA probe selection and inside/outside sampling in separate partition samples.

observable.value: Droplet/turbidity appearance/disappearance, qualitative fluorescence recovery, and background-subtracted confocal DNA-associated signal.

response.value: Cooling forms dense droplets and reheating disperses them with hysteresis. Separate FRAP shows qualitative recovery. Separate partition images enrich ssDNA-associated and deplete dsDNA-associated signal inside droplets.

conditions.value: Thermal: 202 micromolar protein, 200 mM NaCl, pH 8, 50→22 C and reheat at 4 C/min. FRAP: 20 C, nominal 150 mM NaCl; main/SI mixture conflict. Partition: nominal 162.5 micromolar total protein, 150 mM NaCl, 1 micromolar DNA; source K=outside/inside.

resources.value: Supplied purified protein, fluorescent tracers/DNA, buffers and imposed temperature cycles.

boundary.value: Thermal, FRAP and DNA partition are three separate source preparations. This disordered terminal-region system is not a folded-helicase catalytic assay or a universal coacervate model.

timeScale.value: Thermal Figure 3D uses 4 C/min, distinct from 2 C/min cloud-point sampling. FRAP droplet is roughly 10 micrometers. Exact new recovery time/diffusion constant and catalytic observation window are not admitted.

controls.value: Repeated thermal cycles on the same sample; no-DNA fluorescence background; ten inside/ten outside regions in each of three fields in partition assay.

interpretation.value: Reversible source-specific demixing, tracer mobility and fluorescent-solute redistribution are supported. These observables do not establish a catalytic or metabolic advantage.

uncertainty.value: FRAP mixture and DNA dye annotations conflict; no exact new diffusion, partition/free-energy or intrinsic affinity inferred. Functional consequence is unmeasured, not zero.

observations.statement: The same supplied sample demixes during cooling and optically disperses during reheating in repeated source cycles.
A separate source dense-droplet preparation shows qualitative tracer fluorescence recovery after photobleaching.
A separate source assay shows ssDNA-associated signal enrichment and dsDNA-associated signal depletion inside Ddx4 droplets.
No reaction-rate or metabolic benefit is measured in these three admitted preparations.

limitations: Function unknown is not measured zero benefit
FRAP mixture and DNA dye annotations unresolved
No universal threshold, equilibrium criticality, intrinsic DNA affinity, transport rate or catalytic/metabolic gain
Repeated cycles/regions are not independent publications

cases.title: CETCH: composition failure and finite externally supplied cycling

participants.value: Explicit source-main-text-only CETCH 1.0 stepwise and combined preparations, plus the separate externally assembled CETCH 5.4 enzyme network. These are literature-scoped preparation descriptions, not one identified physical system across versions.

changedFactor.value: CETCH 1.0 stepwise enzyme addition versus all components present from the start; later redesigns change several enzymes and support systems. CETCH 5.4 has its own finite isotope/product assay.

observable.value: Main-text source reports of CETCH 1.0 stepwise intermediate conversion and combined non-completion; separate CETCH 5.4 intermediate abundance/isotope-label time courses and coupled malate product readout. Complete 1.0 traces and supplementary controls are not reconstructed.

response.value: The source reports CETCH 1.0 combined-operation stalling at methylsuccinyl-CoA before a full turn, despite stepwise conversion into key intermediates. In the separate supplied CETCH 5.4 assay, intermediates progressively label over 90 minutes and the source reports 540 micromolar malate; its stoichiometric accounting gives 1080 micromolar fixed CO2 and approximately 5 nmol CO2/min/mg core protein.

The admitted case is a supplied and externally assembled in vitro enzyme network. Mature enzymes, cofactors, chemical starting acceptor and resource/regeneration inputs are supplied; it does not synthesize its enzyme catalysts, produce an autonomous cell, or demonstrate collectively autocatalytic production of all network components.

Stepwise conversion in CETCH 1.0 did not establish continuous cycling: the simultaneously combined version stalled before a complete turn at methylsuccinyl-CoA. The main text attributes this to electron-acceptor limitations; the underlying supplementary controls are not newly verified.

CETCH 5.4 has 13 named core reactions plus auxiliary proofreading/cofactor regeneration, with 17 enzymes from nine organisms in the complete source system. Reaction count, enzyme count and biological origins are distinct; they are not universal carrier minima or independently verified assembly stoichiometry.

The principal evidence combines six intermediate abundance/isotopologue time courses with a source-topology interpretation and a coupled malate assay. Glyoxylate is trapped by supplied malate synthase using externally added acetyl-CoA. Malate contains externally supplied carbon and is not itself a product composed solely of the fixed CO2.

Source Figure 2C reports 540 micromolar malate over 90 minutes, corresponding in its two-CO2-per-glyoxylate stoichiometric accounting to 1080 micromolar fixed CO2. The cited approximately 5 nmol CO2 per minute per mg uses core cycle protein, not all supplied proteins. These are source-reported values, not independently reproduced quantities or uncertainties.

Progressive 13C enrichment constrains repeated pathway passage under the declared topology. It does not directly track every individual molecule, prove a global steady state, reveal all side fluxes, certify complete mass balance or establish unbounded throughput. Finite intermediate levels change over the same assay.

Thermodynamic profiles, ATP equivalents and hypothetical photon costs in Table 1 are calculations under adopted stoichiometry, P/O and photophosphorylation assumptions. No calorimetry, complete energy balance, realized photosynthetic coupling or universal energetic superiority follows.

Different CETCH versions alter enzymes, regeneration, protection and side-reaction handling together. No isolated allosteric feedback variable, universally adaptive stabilization mechanism, matched direct comparison with a natural in vivo cycle, or unique causal contribution of each change is admitted.

No long-term robustness under varying conditions, homeostatic flux control, adaptive persistence, membrane transport, autonomous catalyst replacement, origin-of-life sequence or universal requirement for a prior autocatalytic RNA network is measured.
No raw HPLC-MS data replay, model fitting, calibration reconstruction, independent acquisition or laboratory optimization is claimed.

Retain 2:1 myristoleate:monomyristolein as the selected preparation and distinguish nucleotide activation state and the presence or absence of magnesium.
studies.observable: Gel-filtration-separated nucleotide distribution measured by radioactivity or UV absorbance over time.
studies.finding: The selected membrane shows little AMP/ADP/ATP leakage over 24 hours without magnesium; AMP and ADP can permeate slowly with magnesium. Singly charged phosphorimidazolide-activated nucleotides cross more readily, with source-reported equilibration half-time approximately 12 hours under the approximately 100 nm conditions.
limitations: Gel filtration separates vesicle-associated and released solute; leakage from an encapsulated stock is the direct measurement. Extrapolation to external uptake assumes the same passive membrane transport, and the separate encapsulated-primer experiment tests compatibility in its own context.

Negligible AMP/ADP/ATP release over 24 hours without magnesium is a finite detection/time bound, not exact zero permeability or permanent exclusion. Magnesium effects depend on nucleotide complexation; they are not a universal net-charge-only rate law.

The reported approximately 12-hour equilibration half-time is for the source activated-nucleotide/100-nm-vesicle conditions. It is not a fitted transport clock for Zhu micrometre multilamellar vesicles, all nutrients or an in-vivo cell.

The concerted amphiphile-solute inversion and curved intermediate are proposed explanations. No transient lipid-solute complex, elementary flip event or unique microscopic mechanism was directly observed.

studies.system: Finite fluorescent oligonucleotide retention
studies.preparation: The source incorporates supplied fluorescein-labelled dA10 into prepared amphiphile vesicles, removes exterior oligonucleotide by size-exclusion separation and follows released versus vesicle-associated fluorescence. studies.observable: Size-exclusion-separated fluorescent dA10 distribution through the displayed 24-hour window.
studies.finding: Figure S6 shows approximately 100% vesicle-associated fluorescent dA10 over the displayed 24-hour window in the source assay. This supports finite polymer retention alongside separate small-solute permeability observations.
limitations: The retained cargo is supplied fluorescent dA10 DNA, not a replicating genome, folded catalyst, growing autocatalytic network or mixed coacervate compartment.

studies.system: Composition-dependent vesicle ribose permeability
studies.preparation: Compare the source myristoleate-based and other prepared amphiphile vesicles with encapsulated calcein. Ribose addition produces an osmotic volume response recorded by stopped-flow fluorescence at 23 C in POPSO pH 8.2, with the stated EDTA or magnesium alternative. The apparent solute permeability comes from slower volume recovery after initial water efflux; retain membrane composition, vesicle size and sugar-pulse assumptions.
studies.observable: Stopped-flow calcein fluorescence interpreted as shrink-swell vesicle-volume kinetics and apparent solute permeability.
studies.finding: For the selected Table S1 comparison, ribose permeability is reported as 24 for myristoleate and 87 for 2:1 myristoleate:monomyristolein, in units 10^-8 cm/s. Other composition/solute comparisons show conditional variation rather than a universal permeability constant.
limitations: The shrink-swell fluorescence response is interpreted through vesicle-volume/transport assumptions. It is not a direct molecular trajectory, active transport current or independent measurement of a concerted solute-lipid flip.

Table S1 reports central permeability values without a per-entry uncertainty model. Its sugar permeability units are 10^-8 cm/s and water permeability units are 10^-2 cm/s; these columns are not interchangeable. No statistical confidence for a newly calculated fold-change is supplied.

The source uses 0.1 or 0.5 M sugar additions, depending on measurement; the text does not resolve that assignment for every printed table row. Composition comparisons retain that limitation rather than an invented common pulse.

The observed membrane-composition effects do not establish autonomous nutrient/waste regulation, a maintained metabolic steady state, a universal pH law or independently necessary ionic, dispersion or liquid-state causal fractions.

studies.preparation: Source Figure 7 and SI Section S8 separate in vitro Ddx4N1 droplet preparation: nominal total protein 162.5 micromolar, 150 mM NaCl after mixing, 1 micromolar total fluorescent 32-base ssDNA or 32-base-paired dsDNA, with a no-DNA fluorescence background. Confocal emission is volume-normalized across ten inside/ten outside regions in each of three fields. Source K is outside/inside. Main paragraph dye annotation differs from caption/method; no exact partition/free-energy or intrinsic binding constant is newly admitted.
studies.observable: Background-subtracted volume-normalized emission inside/outside Ddx4 droplets for labeled ssDNA/dsDNA
studies.finding: The source reports differential labeled-DNA partition proxies, with no new calibrated binding/free-energy result.
limitations: Read the complete published primary article pages 936-947, complete PMC main HTML and all seven main figures/captions. The author-lab PDF has a graphical cover plus twelve published pages. Read selected actual 29-page publisher supplement: title page, Figure S4 page 5, Figure S7 pages 10-11, Section S2 relevant in vitro/FRAP pages 14-16, Section S6 pages 21-25, and Section S8 pages 27-28. In vitro terminal-region phase separation is not a demonstration of native germ-granule function, helicase catalysis or a universal folded-protein prerequisite.

Thermal Figure 3D reports 202 micromolar Ddx4N1, 200 mM NaCl and pH 8, with cooling/heating and same-sample repeats. Its 4 degrees C/min demonstration differs from the 2 degrees C/min default cloud-point sampling in SI Section S6. Cooling appearance and reheating disappearance differ; an operational image/turbidity threshold is not independently established equilibrium criticality or a universal minimum molecule count.

Cloud-point data and Flory-Huggins/screened-Coulomb fits are separate from direct images. Assumptions about polymer volume fraction, water, effective interaction constants and electrostatic screening underlie fitted enthalpy/entropy, charge spacing and dielectric values. No new direct molecular force, solvent structure, dielectric or calorimetric measurement is admitted.

No exact common composition or ratio is silently selected. The qualitative recovery trace is admitted, with no new precise diffusion coefficient.

FRAP recovery depends on bleach geometry, imaging, diffusion/exchange assumptions and the fluorescent tracer. It supports mobility in the reported droplet preparation, not all constituent dynamics, DNA transport kinetics, viscosity, universal liquid character or proof that every condensate/coacervate has the same mechanism.

No numerical partition/free-energy value, unlabeled-DNA binding constant, universal sequence specificity or corrected dye identity is independently admitted.

Ten inside/ten outside regions in each of three fields of view are sampling regions, not automatically sixty independent preparation replications. SD of emission regions and model-fit SE are different uncertainties. No independent replication or raw-image replay is performed.

Cellular cold/osmotic response, methylated/splice/charge/aromatic variants and genome enrichment were read but are not new admitted assay contexts. Cellular osmotic changes alter volume/concentration and environment together; sequence/general-mechanism hypotheses do not become universal proof for all condensates.

No direct catalytic reaction modulation, metabolic throughput/benefit, universal reaction sequestration, membrane-like selectivity, gradient maintenance, prebiotic coacervate ancestry or origin-of-life event is measured in the admitted contexts.

studies.system: Isolated CAPN/cAMP calorimetric titration in high-salt pH6 phosphate buffer
studies.preparation: At30C titrate0.6mM cAMP into a30micromolar CAPN preparation using a VP-ITC instrument after dialysis into50mM potassium phosphate pH6.0,500mM KCl and1mM TCEP. Ligand is prepared in the final buffer-exchange flow-through. Discard the preliminary2microliter injection and use the subsequent30 eight-microliter injections. Fit the integrated isotherm using the sequential binding-site model in Origin7.0; NMR preparations use different stated protein concentrations and are not treated as the same physical sample.
studies.observable: Injection heat versus time and integrated heat per injectant/protein ratio, fitted with a sequential-site binding model
studies.finding: The source reports first/second sequential Kd0.04/4micromolar and enthalpy/total-entropy compensation favoring weaker second-step binding; these are fitted, convention-dependent quantities with no reconstructed uncertainties.
limitations: This source studies an expressed, purified His6-tagged E. coli CAP N-terminal fragment comprising residues1-138. It lacks the C-terminal DNA-binding domain of full-length CAP; no DNA binding, transcription, catalytic turnover, cellular adaptation or physiological response is measured in this selected study.

The protein is supplied as a prepared homodimer. Its composition and two cAMP-binding positions are system-specific inputs/assignments, not a universal two-molecule threshold or proof that all allostery requires oligomerization.

The source supplies a ligand-series experiment at30C and fixed assay protocols. It does not measure a universal folding, hydrogen-bond, electrostatic, hydration or feedback ancestry, and it does not operationalize original parent weights or carrier minima.

The supporting information, raw NMR/ITC acquisition, complete concentration calibration, original fitting implementation and covariance are not independently reviewed or reproduced. All admitted quantities retain publication-supported status.

Figure7 constants are source sequential-binding fit parameters, not a Hill coefficient, direct atom-count measurement or new microscopic site-specific constants. Sequential constants require their combinatorial/state convention before translating them into intrinsic coupling energies; no statistical-factor correction is newly calculated here.

A biphasic isotherm or nonlinearity alone does not uniquely establish intersite communication rather than fixed site heterogeneity. The source interpretation also uses the symmetric-dimer preparation and site-resolved ligand-series NMR.

The reported0.04 and4micromolar constants have no printed uncertainty in Figure7; none is invented. The100-fold ratio and rounded thermodynamic entries are source statements, not a new fit or uncertainty reconstruction.

The main manuscript gives protein concentrations without a separately reconstructed monomer/dimer concentration calibration. Its intended dimer ligation states are retained, but the Figure7 molar-ratio axis is not used as an independent site-count determination.

Nominal cAMP:CAPN dimer ratios1:1 and2:1 enrich the source-assigned ligation states; finite affinities and stoichiometric mixing do not demonstrate mathematically pure occupancy populations. The source complete-saturation phrasing is not promoted to a new measured purity guarantee.

The manuscript prose prints an enthalpy-difference expression with a repeated first index; the distinct Figure7 entries are the admitted source values. Rounded displayed free-energy, heat and entropy entries do not supply exact covariance or separate microscopic coupling energy.
Both binding steps have favorable total entropy terms in Figure7. A less favorable second-step entropy is not the same as unfavorable total entropy of that step.

Chemical shifts report local electronic environments and population averages. Small shifts at the remote cAMP pocket constrain a large mean-environment change under this method; they do not prove exact structural identity, an absence of every atom displacement or purely entropy-only causation.

Existing cAMP-bound CAP structure1G6N supplies molecular models, mapping coordinates and distances; it is not a new three-state atomic structure determination. Unread earlier structure data are not cloned as new experiments.

Relaxation-derived spectral densities, exchange rates and order parameters are model-dependent inferences from NMR signals. In the fast-exchange analysis only kex and pA*pB*(deltaomega)^2 are separately accessible; the excited-state population and shift difference are not independently identified.

The nominal ligation-state comparison is controlled within the source experiment, but exact purity of the assigned singly/doubly liganded populations has not been independently measured here. Concentration controls constrain aggregation under tested conditions, not every alternative process.

Conformational entropy is inferred using reduced spectral densities, exchange-corrected T2, local rotational times and the source order-parameter-to-entropy mapping. Backbone amplitudes, correlations, unmeasured motions and solvent/ligand entropy restrict quantitative interpretation.

The article expressly treats its conformational entropy estimate as an upper bound because it assumes motions are uncorrelated. Its own discussion invokes favorable solvation entropy; total ITC entropy is not a direct measurement of protein-only entropy.

A dynamic response, an entropic balance and an undetected mean-shift response do not uniquely rule out all structural, solvent or electrostatic contributions, prove a universal mechanism, or discriminate all MWC/KNF/landscape descriptions.

Original Level3, Phase2(Self-organization), TypeRole3(Property), Science arrays and established/well-supported labels are catalogue/display declarations. They do not validate a separate arising, persistent ontological disposition, global-to-local causal hierarchy or ordered molecular construction.

Original MustCover substrate/constraint [0,10], ShouldCover regulation/environment [4,12], Optional gradient/information [5,7] are not empirical gates. Actual construct, ligand, salt, pH and temperature are retained; no universal maintained gradient, information variable, feedback loop or resource architecture is demonstrated.

Generic original MWC, KNF, conformational-selection and landscape references carry no specific publication identity. These mechanisms are not equated and none is newly selected, fitted or proven. The chosen experiment does not identify a unique microscopic pathway.

No numerical parent weight, universal necessity, counted molecule minimum, critical threshold or saturation count is admitted. A dimer and two ligands in this case specify a preparation/model, not a universal hierarchy or minimal carrier theorem.
The same publication and two distinct assay preparations support all three card scopes. They are not independent confirmations, and NMR model-based entropy is not a third independent acquisition.

Original site/subunit energetic coupling is qualified to source-defined CAPN binding/dynamics. The selected result is negative homotropic coupling; positive cooperativity, sensitivity amplification, sigmoid switching, threshold response and generalized catalytic coordination are not measured by this case.

A nonlinear response is not sufficient by itself to establish cooperativity. No Hill coefficient, integer site inference from a Hill exponent, mutational coupling pathway or validated mechanical propagation chain is supplied.

Original parents3.0 folding(weight0.4,necessary,constraint),3.1 enzymatic catalysis(0.3,enabling,regulation),3.2 active sites(0.2,enabling,constraint),2.7 hydrogen bonds(0.1,contextual,constraint) have horizontal direction[2] and cooperation/feedback/constraint modes as catalogued. Prepared CAPN supplies no universal necessity or those weights; cAMP binding in the isolated fragment is not catalytic turnover.

Every3.5 parent uses functional-material/molecule carrier2/4,N_min=N_crit=1,N_sat=null. No operational carrier threshold is measured, and a recurrent equilibrium interaction is not proof of a temporal feedback cycle.

Original ligand-induced distal response is qualified to CAPN binding, relaxation and exchange in the selected construct. Covalent regulatory modification, catalytic accessibility, altered catalytic activity, general conformational stability, adaptive response, multi-signal integration and living-system regulation are not measured here.

The source supports effects on motions with limited remote mean-shift response. It does not establish that all allostery requires a large conformational change, that one particular microscopic pathway is necessary, or that every folded protein has this regulatory property.

studies.system: trans-H-C-OH / H-C-OD cryogenic matrix rearrangement to formaldehyde
studies.preparation: Generate hydroxymethylene by high-vacuum flash pyrolysis of glyoxylic acid at 1000 deg C and immediately co-condense the products with excess Ar, Kr, Xe or N2 on a cryogenic window. Unreacted precursor, CO2, formaldehyde and some CO are also present. Assign trans-H-C-OH and H-C-OD using infrared/UV observations and computed vibrational bands. For dark kinetics, shield external light and acquire infrared spectra every 30 min at the reported 11, 15 or 20 K settings, following the approximately 1050 and 1300 cm^-1 H-C-OH bands.
studies.observable: Decrease of assigned hydroxymethylene infrared bands versus elapsed dark-storage time; separate visible-light difference spectra support assignment but are not the dark kinetics.
studies.finding: The source reports first-order H-C-OH loss and the following half-lives in hours: at 11 K Ar 1.8, Kr 2.0, Xe 2.3 and N2 7.0; at 15 K Ar 1.9; at 20 K Ar 1.7 and Kr 2.0. Other temperature/matrix entries in Supplementary Table 1 are explicitly not determined. H-C-OD infrared bands are reported unchanged for an unspecified extended observation period. The approximately two-hour summary applies to the reported noble-gas preparations, while the 11 K nitrogen matrix is slower by more than a factor of three.
limitations: No uncertainty intervals, replicate counts or detection limit are given in Supplementary Table 1; none is invented. Not-determined cells remain missing, not zero or interpolated.

The deuterated observation window is not numerically stated, so no experimental D half-life, lower bound in years or numerical kinetic isotope ratio is inferred. Over 1200 yr belongs only to the separate calculation.
The 435/470/500 nm irradiation tests and the two-minute 470 nm difference spectra probe a driven photochemical response and species assignment. They are not the shielded dark decay measurement.

The sample is a product mixture in a cryogenic matrix, not a pure isolated-molecule gas. Infrared assignment and dilution arguments do not directly count individual tunnelling events, certify every initial quantum state or exclude every possible loss channel by direct observation.

The reported matrix and temperature dependence does not establish a universal vacuum lifetime, a measured 0 K rate or a carrier-number threshold. No raw spectral refit or independent numerical replay was performed.

studies.system: Ground-singlet trans-H-C-OH to H2CO reduced reaction-path tunnelling
studies.preparation: Use the ground-electronic-singlet trans-H-C-OH to H2CO channel with AE-CCSD(T)/cc-pCVQZ stationary structures and focal-point energy corrections. Construct the intrinsic reaction path and orthogonal harmonic frequencies at AE-CCSD/cc-pCVTZ and refine path energies at AE-CCSD(T)/cc-pCVQZ. Apply a reduced reaction-path Hamiltonian with WKB transmission at the reaction-mode zero-point energy, using the 1220 cm^-1 reactant harmonic mode and its corresponding barrier-attempt frequency. The same procedure is applied to H-C-OD; an asymmetric Eckart calculation is a separate qualitative check.
studies.observable: Source-computed ground-vibrational-level tunnelling half-lives and explicitly approximation-dependent reaction-profile energies; not a newly measured kinetic curve.
studies.finding: The source reduced reaction-path/WKB calculation predicts a near-0-K H-C-OH half-life of 122 min, reported as 2.0 h, and a H-C-OD half-life over 1200 yr. These are theoretical outputs. Figure 4 uses focal-point plus harmonic zero-point energies relative to CO+H2: trans reactant 54.2 and TS2 83.9 kcal/mol, with the displayed difference 29.7 kcal/mol; the trans anharmonic value is 54.0. A separate Eckart check uses a stated 31.60 kcal/mol barrier, -52.05 kcal/mol reaction energy and 2174i cm^-1 imaginary transition-state wavenumber. These printed model inputs have distinct conventions and are not merged into one experimental barrier.
limitations: This is the source-reported calculation associated with the same publication as the experiment; it is not an independent empirical confirmation or an independently reproduced numerical check.

The calculation uses a reduced reaction-path approximation. The paper explicitly leaves full-dimensional quantum dynamics on a semi-global potential surface for future work; neither an exact full-dimensional rate nor a direct trajectory is admitted.
No matrix-specific potential or environmental kinetic fit for all four hosts is supplied by this admission; the 7.0 h nitrogen result does not become a 2.0 h model validation.

The 29.7 kcal/mol Figure 4 harmonic-zero-point schematic difference is not a bare electronic barrier and is not substituted for the separately printed 31.60 kcal/mol Eckart-model input. No unresolved mapping between approximations is invented.

The over-1200-year deuterium prediction has no numerical experimental confirmation in the reported observation period. Quantized energy references and barrier transmission are different parts of the inference.

studies.observable: Agarose/TEM morphology, dye colocalization and normalized photobleaching/label counts
studies.finding: The source supports an enzyme-associated DNA-cage population, with proxy/calibration limits rather than universal exact pair occupancy.
limitations: This is a synthetic DNA-origami scaffold carrying commercially supplied enzymes, not a naturally evolved protein-only multienzyme complex, living metabolic network, protein biosynthesis or a cellular-origin experiment. The scaffold DNA is supplied; its sequence-dependent assembly was not independently reconstructed.

Negatively stained TEM, dye colocalization and photobleaching report different preparations/proxies. They support source-defined loading and location, not exact atom-level interfaces, universal pair occupancy, an impermeable shell or a measured protein-protein channel.

Photobleaching copy-number estimates normalize detected Cy3 steps to labels per free enzyme and depend on labeling, detection and six-state HMM assumptions. TableS3 covers HRP, G6pDH and beta-Gal, not direct proof that every cascade cage has exactly one GOx and one HRP.

Bulk cage concentration uses A260 and an adopted extinction coefficient0.109 nM^-1cm^-1; conjugate concentrations/labeling use absorbance deconvolution and inherited coefficients. Calibration, gel-extraction losses, active-enzyme fractions and labeling are not independently reproduced.

GOx/HRP activity is a coupled ABTS absorbance readout. It depends on both enzyme steps, intermediate availability, substrate concentrations and active fractions; it is not an isolated turnover count, direct intermediate trajectory, flux control coefficient or exclusive measure of substrate transfer.

The source nominally matches enzyme/cage concentrations but paired, separately caged and uncaged preparations differ in assembly, conjugation, purification, local environment and total cage/DNA organization. No isolated geometric confinement variable or equal active-site population is proven.

Separate full cages and half-cages also increase the coupled signal. Increased activity of a co-caged pair therefore does not uniquely establish direct substrate channeling, reduced intermediate escape or a proximity-only mechanism.

Hydration-layer ordering, electrostatic stabilization and conformational-substate mechanisms are proposed interpretations. Salt/helix-density comparisons alter more than one property and do not directly measure local water structure, local pH or a unique mechanism.

The single-molecule G6pDH enzymology uses a different enzyme, surface immobilization, PMS/resazurin reporter and 10 percent PEG. It is not the same GOx/HRP bulk cascade preparation or an independent replication of its fold enhancement.

The main/SI trypsin protocol annotations differ in digestion buffer, pH, enzyme concentration and assay ABTS concentration. No new protection/aggregation or persistence claim is admitted from those conflicting annotations.

No crosstalk suppression, competing-pathway insulation, local concentration gradient, intermediate residence/retention, synchronized feedback, closed metabolic cycle, sustained living-system regulation or universal efficiency benefit is measured in the admitted contexts.

families.title: Conditions and organizational regimes
families.eligibility: A declared intervention or computational scan changes a specified condition and reports a discriminating structural/order observable. Keep model ensembles separate from physical preparations; distinguish jointly changed conditions from an isolated causal intervention.
families.scopedPrediction: Within the specified comparison, the reported condition change selects distinguishable states under the stated organizational observable. This is a case-specific retrospective prediction; it assigns no universal threshold and predicts no unmeasured dynamics.

supportCriteria.text: The source reports distinct organizational readouts under the declared conditions, with preparation and observation/model boundaries retained.

contraryCriteria.text: Within an eligible matched test, the specified discriminator remains unchanged across the claimed switching range at the declared resolution. Such a result challenges that bounded prediction, not all possible condition dependence.

inconclusiveCriteria.text: Readouts are absent, conditions/constructs change together, or a model-assisted classification does not isolate the proposed physical switching mechanism.

families.overextension: A component list uniquely fixes organization, every environmental change induces a transition, or a phase label alone supplies physical kinetics.

families.title: Persistence through barriers, exchange constraints and supplied resources
families.eligibility: Specify what persists or recovers, its preparation, a perturbation/comparator if available, and a finite observation window. Separate measured durations, fitted/extrapolated rates and computational clocks. Barrier, exchange and replenishment hypotheses are different mechanisms.
families.scopedPrediction: A specified target remains detectable or recurrently operational over the reported finite horizon under the stated boundary/resource conditions; loss or altered persistence in a relevant comparison constrains its maintenance requirements. Mechanism identification requires additional controls.

supportCriteria.text: The source establishes finite retention, limited conversion, recovery or repeated operation under declared conditions, without converting non-detection or extrapolation into indefinite stability.

Data-dependent rate fits/extrapolations support a preparation-conditional kinetic persistence account with the measured input, model and uncertainty retained. This is evidence about inferred kinetics; no direct observation of the extrapolated lifetime is claimed.

contraryCriteria.text: An actually reported loss, stall or depletion contradicts the overextension from topology, structural order or individually working steps to unconditional persistent operation. Do not label missing measurements as observed loss.

inconclusiveCriteria.text: Persistence horizon is unmeasured, the relevant control is missing, a lifetime is extrapolated, or the evidence does not isolate a claimed barrier, exchange or replenishment mechanism.

families.overextension: A cycle is autonomous, every ordered structure persists indefinitely, a fitted extrapolation is an observed lifetime, or all persistence mechanisms share one numerical stability measure.

families.title: Organization-associated changes in operation
families.eligibility: Require a declared functional/response observable and a comparator. State the anticipated direction or qualitative discriminator for each case; preserve active fractions, preparation differences and possible common-environment explanations.
families.scopedPrediction: In the selected matched comparison, the declared state/arrangement change is associated with its specified response difference (including sign reversal or suppression). Spatial proximity alone cannot identify a mechanism or predict improvement.

supportCriteria.text: An actual comparison reports the named response difference under stated controls. This supports only that scoped response relation, not a unique pathway or universal benefit.

contraryCriteria.text: A measured suppressive, null or sign-changing response challenges a universal monotonic-gain extension. Do not treat a missing functional assay as a measured null.

The source reports successful individual transformations but incomplete operation when combined, challenging guaranteed composition of working steps. Keep the preparation and actual extent of failure/control review explicit.

inconclusiveCriteria.text: Only structure, partition, mobility or pair interaction is measured; the proposed functional benefit or assembly operation is not measured.
A response difference exists but alternative controls, unmatched active populations or multiple changed conditions prevent attribution to the proposed isolated mechanism.
A functional outcome is measured, but no matched organizational comparator identifies an organization-specific change or benefit. Observed operation alone is insufficient for this candidate.

families.overextension: More organization necessarily improves operation, co-localization proves substrate channeling, or partition alone demonstrates catalytic benefit.

links.correspondence: Both cases distinguish organizational states using a declared control series and observable rather than component count alone.
links.breakdownConditions: A two-dimensional equilibrium hard-disk computation and a hysteretic protein solution have different interactions, ensembles and readouts. No packing threshold, physical clock or phase mechanism transfers.

links.correspondence: Different external preparations select distinct source-assigned states with distinguishable readouts.
links.breakdownConditions: Protein spectra/construct assays and constrained film polarity/response require different state coordinates. No shared microscopic switching mechanism or isolated structure-to-function cause is asserted.

links.correspondence: Both cases require persistence to be conditional on preparation and observation/inference method; structural order or function does not establish a thermodynamic ground state.
links.breakdownConditions: Finite alloy anneals and extrapolated protein rates provide different evidence. No measured common barrier, universal minimum or numerical lifetime transfer is available.

links.breakdownConditions: Matrix-host isotope-dependent chemical conversion and protein folding/unfolding are distinct targets and mechanisms. WKB predictions are not protein-barrier measurements; the unreported D horizon and protein extrapolations remain unresolved.

links.correspondence: Persistence questions require explicit resource and exchange boundaries: selective cargo retention differs from replenished catalytic amplification.
links.breakdownConditions: The separate vesicle assays are not the RNA ligation preparation. The analogy makes no claim that these chemistries already compose into one protocell or that confinement is required for ligation.

links.breakdownConditions: Protein-enzyme carbon fixation and reciprocal RNA ligation have different outputs, activation resources and turnover definitions. Neither supplies the other's inputs or proves autonomous catalyst/resource manufacture.

links.correspondence: Specified organization/state comparisons change measured responses, with enhancement and suppression requiring distinct observables and controls.
links.breakdownConditions: Coupled enzyme absorbance and sequential ligand affinity/NMR response are not a common performance scale. Neither identifies a shared communication/channeling mechanism.

links.breakdownConditions: Ddx4 has no admitted catalytic-benefit assay, whereas the cage case has a coupled activity comparison with confounds. No functional equivalence or liquid-like cage mechanism is proposed.

review.retrospectiveExposure: All selected publications and reported outcomes were available during source review and informed this purposive selection and protocol. No case in this pilot is a genuinely unseen prospective test. Case annotations are literature interpretations, not independent acquisition or numerical replay.
review.splitRationale: Keep each primary publication and its preparation/readout/model records in one dependency group. Use AlScN switching, the isolated colloid-pair null, all CETCH versions and all selected Mansy vesicle preparations as retrospective challenge groups; the other ten publication groups develop the comparisons. Group disjointness is a leakage check, not proof that different publications have no shared assumptions or that the selection is representative.
review.currentConclusion:
The selected cases support several bounded distinctions rather than one universal organization law. Conditions discriminate organizational regimes in particular models/preparations; retention, kinetic resistance and supplied recurrent operation have different evidential requirements; state or arrangement changes can alter measured response without demonstrating a universal efficiency gain.

Contrary and unresolved cases are central results: CETCH 1.0 does not compose from working steps into a complete recurrent turn; batch RNA amplification depletes supplied substrates; negative CAPN cooperativity limits a universal amplification interpretation; isolated colloid data do not establish long-range attraction; Ddx4 partition does not measure catalytic benefit; and cage controls do not uniquely identify substrate channeling. These distinctions motivate conditional compatibility and maintenance hypotheses, not a new physical ancestry chain.

Retrospective challenge cases expose limits of transfer: AlScN supplies a state-associated response sign change in a specific film preparation; CETCH contrasts designed topology with supplied finite operation and a reported earlier stall; vesicles separate exchange, retention and primer-extension assays; and the colloid-pair null prevents treating every interaction measurement as assembly evidence. No common numerical threshold, causal/emergence score, prospective generalization result or independently reviewed scientific conclusion follows.

Separate new-source readings of Banerjee2017, Boekhoven2015 and Drobot2018 test the operational distinctions outside the selected atlas publications. These checks retain the case-specific readout, comparator and limitations; their result-bearing titles/search exposure and retrospective target selection prevent a blind prospective validation claim. Full review records remain outside canonical physical-claim admission.
